exercises.title: Hello, ratatui
exercises.guide: Build the smallest ratatui app: it draws one line of text and quits when you press any key.

chunks.guide: Import the main pieces the app needs from ratatui.

notes.text: Lets the app read key presses.
The terminal your app draws in.

chunks.guide: `main` only starts ratatui. `app` is written next.

notes.text: Prepares the terminal, runs app, then restores the terminal.

chunks.guide: `app` gets the terminal. Every terminal app loops: **draw**, then **wait for an event**.
`draw` calls `render` with a `Frame`, then shows the result on screen.
`event::read` waits for an event. Any key press ends the app.
`render` only draws; it never reads keys. A plain string is already a widget.

notes.text: Draws a widget inside an area.

exercises.title: A Paragraph
exercises.guide: A plain string works, but most of the time you draw a **widget** from `ratatui::widgets`. `Paragraph` is the simplest one: it shows text and can align it. The output is drawn for a 30-column terminal.

chunks.guide: `Frame` is already in the file. Widgets live in `ratatui::widgets`.
`render` is already in the file. Methods that return the widget can be chained: the **builder style** used all over ratatui.
Same call as before, now with a `Paragraph`.

exercises.title: The frame area
exercises.guide: `frame.area()` is a `Rect`: the position and size of the whole terminal. Widgets draw **inside** a `Rect`, so knowing the area is the first step to placing anything. The output is drawn for an 80 by 24 terminal.

chunks.guide: The import and `render` are already in the file. A `Rect` has four fields: `x`, `y`, `width` and `height`.
`width` and `height` are measured in **cells**: one cell holds one character.
chunks.text: let size = format!("{} x {}", area.width, area.height);

chunks.guide: A `String` is a widget too. Draw it in the full area.

exercises.title: Two widgets
exercises.guide: One frame can hold many widgets. Each one gets its own `Rect`, built with `Rect::new(x, y, width, height)`, where `x` and `y` count cells from the top-left corner.

chunks.guide: `Frame` is already in the file. `Rect` lives in `ratatui::layout`, with everything about placing widgets.
The other import and `render` are already in the file. Creating a widget only **describes** it: nothing is on screen yet.
chunks.text:
let title = Paragraph::new("Title");
    let body = Paragraph::new("Body");

chunks.guide: Each widget is drawn in its own `Rect`. Row 1 stays empty.

exercises.title: Draw again on every key
exercises.guide: `app` draws, waits for a key, and loops, so it draws **again after every event**. What `render` shows can change between frames. Here the screen counts key presses, and `q` quits. The output is the screen after three key presses.

chunks.guide: `Event` is what `event::read` returns, and `KeyCode` names a key.
`DefaultTerminal` and `Frame` are already imported. `presses` lives outside the loop, so it keeps its value between frames: the app's **state**.
`draw` gets a closure so `presses` can be passed to `render`.
`event::read` returns an `Event`. We only care about key events.
`q` ends the program.
Any other key adds one. The loop then draws again with the new number.

`render` only reads the state, it never changes it.

State in `app`, drawing in `render`: the base of every larger ratatui program.
